NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv . For more information, please contact the City Clerk''s office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to the regular City Council meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk''s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk’s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the City's system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. Agendas are available at the following locations:

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING

  July 27, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER

The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 5:25 p.m. on July
27, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember  Larry Agran
  Councilmember  Mike Carroll*
  Councilmember  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor  Tammy Kim
  Mayor  Farrah N. Khan
  *Via teleconference

Chairwoman Khan announced that City Hall was now open to the public, allowing
members of the public to physically attend and participate in City Council meetings, and
noted the current guidelines for face coverings. She also noted that 1) the meeting was
broadcast live on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse
Channel 99, and livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; 2) members of the public would
continue to have the ability to provide live comments on agenda items via Zoom; and 3)
the City of Irvine continued to sanitize surfaces and equipment in the Council Chamber
and throughout City Hall.

In addition, Carl Petersen, City Clerk, provided instructions on how to participate in the
meeting; and noted that the e-comment feature had been extended, which allowed
members of the public the ability to submit e-comments on all agenda items, which
would be included as part of the official record and uploaded to the City’s website.

Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.
 City Council Minutes  July 27, 2021

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Agran led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Pastor Jim Gwatlney from Light of Christ Lutheran Church of Irvine provided the
  invocation.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Commendation Recognizing the STARTALK Program

  Mayor Khan introduced students and teachers who participated in the
  StarTalk Program and presented a commendation.

  Vice Mayor Kim expressed her appreciation to the National Foreign
  Language Center and the National Security Agency for providing Irvine
  students an opportunity to learn languages critical to national security.

  RECESS

  Mayor Khan recessed the City Council meeting at 5:36 p.m.

  RECONVENE

  Mayor Khan reconvened the City Council meeting at 5:59 p.m.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Kuo expressed best wishes to all those competing in the Olympics,
  including the men’s and women’s water polo teams whose headquarters is based in
  Irvine; and Irvine natives Amber Neben (cyclist) and Jack Williams (archery).

  Councilmember Agran reiterated his prior requests for support to agendize for
  discussion the following items on the August 10, 2021, City Council meeting agenda for
  City Council discussion:

  1) Veteran’s Memorial Park and Cemetery project;
  2) District Elections; and
  3) City Council Policy for Councilmembers to place items on the City Council
  agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  July 27, 2021

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, clarified that a motion to add items to a future agenda under
  this item would not be the appropriate vehicle to do so; however, Councilmember Agran
  could ask for support from his colleagues to place these items on future agendas.

  Councilmember Kuo offered his support to agendize the matter of district elections as a
  Closed Session item given the potential threat of litigation.

  Councilmember Carroll announced that the Southern California Associations of
  Governments had completed its Regional Housing Needs Assessment plan, and that
  the City of Irvine received the sixth largest allocation of housing in Southern California
  totaling 50,000 units.

  Mayor Khan made the following announcements:

  •  The Irvine Community Television (ICTV) team was recently recognized for
  outstanding government communications. The team, which creates videos and
  programming for the City’s television station, social media, and City events,
  received eight Star Awards from the States of California and Nevada Association
  of Telecommunications Officers and Advisors. ICTV received four 1st place
  awards for: 1) Event coverage of the Wildland Management Event; 2) The
  Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon Public Service Announcement; 3) The 2021 State of
  the City Address; and 4) Virtual event coverage of the 2020 Holiday Tree
  Lighting. ICTV also received three 2nd place awards and one 3rd place award in
  a variety of categories, including Environmental, Public Affairs, Talk Show, and
  Senior Citizen Audience. ICTV can be viewed on Cox Communications Channel
  30, on AT&T U-verse  Channel 99, cityofirvine.org/ictv, and at
  youtube.com/ictv30.

  •  As part of the City’s commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, a number of
  new initiatives are being implemented, which include the following:

   City staff has developed an outreach and training program for women-
  owned and minority-owned businesses. The training program will expand
  awareness of the City’s bidding opportunities, how to get started and
  register as a vendor, procurement processes, and more. Numerous
  training dates are available. Visit cityofirvine.org/purchasing for more
  information, and select a training date and time.

   A new invoice payment portal has also been developed to provide
  residents and businesses with an easy way to make online payments.
  The new user-friendly service allows customers to view unpaid invoices,
  such as false alarm fees and special event reimbursements, and make
  partial or full payments using a secure third-party site. To access the
  portal, visit cityofirvine.org/transparency.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  July 27, 2021

   Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been an increase in the
  use of third-party food delivery services. In order to make third-party
  delivery services more affordable for consumers and to reduce the
  impacts to retail food establishments, the City Council approved an
  ordinance establishing limitations of third-party food delivery fees. A portal
  was created where community members can report ordinance violations
  using a simple online form. To view the ordinance and submit a violation,
  visit cityofirvine.org/covid19 and click on Executive Orders, Resolutions,
  and Ordinances.

  •  Ten years ago, the Palm Court Arts Complex opened at the Orange County Great
  Park, bringing more public, accessible art to the community. To celebrate its 10th
  anniversary, and the community is invited to a special reception for the Great
  Park Gallery’s summer exhibition, Chuck Jones: Season of Creativity. The
  exhibition explores the process of animation from script to screen through original
  art and writing by Chuck Jones, who brought to life some of the most famous
  Warner Bros.’ characters. Invited the community attend the reception on Sunday,
  August 1, at noon at the Great Park Gallery. Attendees can meet renowned
  Disney animator, director, and Chuck Jones protégée Eric Goldberg, as well as
  members of Jones’ family, including: 1) Craig Kausen, chairman of the Chuck
  Jones Center for Creativity, and 2) Chuck Jones’ grandson, a longtime Irvine
  resident. Photos can be taken near the iconic memorabilia, including one of
  Jones’ Oscars and the actual desk he used during his career to create characters
  such as Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Marvin the Martian, Wile E. Coyote, and the
  Road Runner. Afterward, attendees can enjoy the Chuck Jones Lecture & Film
  Series event from 1 to 3 p.m. at Hangar 244. The event is free. No registration
  is required, and all ages are welcome. For information, visit
  cityofirvine.org/chuckjones.

  •  The Irvine Police Department will once again host National Night Out at three
  locations across the City: Woodbury Community Park, Turtle Rock Community
  Park, and Mike Ward Community Park – Woodbridge. National Night Out, a
  highly anticipated summer tradition, will take place on Tuesday, August 3 from
  5:30 to 7:30 p.m. The community is invited to attend the free event featuring
  police vehicles and fire engines, appearances by the Mounted, SWAT, and K9
  Units, Drone Team demonstrations, crime prevention tips, face painting, and
  other activities for kids. Food trucks will have items available for purchase, and
  kids get a free IPD police fidget toy while supplies last.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  July 27, 2021

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Prior to approval of the Consent Calendar, Mayor Khan noted an errata memo
  received for Item 2.3, which included a slight modification to Action Item No. 3.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, and
  unanimously carried to approve Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1 through 2.3.

  2.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minutes of the special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on June 22, 2021.
  2) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council and special joint meeting with the Orange County Great
  Park Board held on June 22, 2021.

  2.2  WARRANT AND WIRE TRANSFER RESOLUTION

  ACTION:
  Adopted RESOLUTION NO. 21-44 - A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE
  FUNDS OUT OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID

  2.3  APPROVAL OF PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS, AND CONTRACT
  DOCUMENTS FOR ORANGE COUNTY GREAT PARK PALM COURT
  STOCKPILE RELOCATION

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the construction plans, specifications, and contract
  documents for the Orange County Great Park Palm Court
  Stockpile Relocation, Capital Improvement Project 361812.
  2) Approved the Engineer’s Estimate, Construction Contingency,
  and Project Funding Summary.
  3) Authorized staff to solicit competitive bids.*

  * Amended per errata memo dated July 26, 2021, to remove the following
  language:

  “…and award the construction contract to the lowest responsive and
  responsible bidder, in accordance with the City’s purchasing policies
  and procedures, within the approved project budget.”

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  July 27, 2021

  3.  COUNCIL BUSINESS

  3.1  CONSIDERATION OF A REQUEST BY COUNCILMEMBER KUO
  AND COUNCILMEMBER CARROLL TO DISCUSS THE
  INSTALLATION OF AN IDENTIFICATION MARKER AT THE
  BARTON MOUND HISTORIC SITE

  This item was agendized at the request of Councilmembers Kuo and
  Carroll, who provided a brief history of the historic site, and requested
  City Council support for the installation of an identification marker
  placed in a visible location for the public to recognize it along the San
  Diego Creek Trail on the Los Olivos side of California Interstate 405
  within the vicinity of Barton Mound.

  Tim Gehrich, Deputy Director of Community Development, provided a
  brief presentation and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: noting the significance of the site’s
  local history; inquired about the potential costs related to the installation
  of the marker; and suggested that consideration be given to the
  perspectives of the all the people involved to ensure that the true history
  of the site and related events is respected.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kuo, and seconded by
  Councilmember Carroll, and unanimously carried to:

  Direct staff to evaluate an appropriate location along the San
  Diego Creek Trail and return with design considerations for the
  identification marker.

  3.2  EMERGENCY RENTAL ASSISTANCE  PROGRAM  ROUND  2
  AUTHORIZATION TO PARTICIPATE

  Keri Bullock, Neighborhood Services Administrator, and Andrew
  Douglass, Interim Housing Manager, presented the staff report and
  responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: requesting clarification about rent
  relief available to University of California Irvine students; inquired about
  options available for the distribution of funds; inquired about when and
  where applications would be available; and noted that an emergency
  rental assistance hotline had been created to assist residents with the
  program.

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the Emergency
  Rental Assistance Program, and suggested the City continue to provide
  regular COVID-19 updates.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  6
 City Council Minutes  July 27, 2021

  Kellie Odom inquired about the availability of applications, and
  expressed concern about the potential public disclosure of personal
  information contained within applications.

  ACTION: Moved by Mayor Khan, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, and
  unanimously carried to:

  Adopt RESOLUTION NO. 21-45 – A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA,
  AUTHORIZING PARTICIPATION IN THE STATE RENTAL
  ASSISTANCE PROGRAM - 2

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  The following individuals spoke in support of the veteran’s cemetery at the Amended
  and Restated Development Agreement (ARDA) site:

  •  Gail Lewis, Irvine resident
  •  Janel Roshmann, Irvine resident
  •  Dee Fox, Irvine resident
  •  Ed McNew, Irvine resident
  •  Steve Clark
  •  Joyce Kassouf, Irvine resident
  •  Harvey Liss, Irvine resident
  •  Don Geller, Irvine resident
  •  Mike Chamberlin
  •  Steve Burger, Irvine resident
  •  Patricia Kennedy

  Michelle Johnson expressed opposition to a veteran’s cemetery at Gypsum Canyon site
  in Anaheim.

  Ashton Gilbert and Emily Nguyen, Green Ribbon Environmental Committee Youth
  Members, spoke in support of a bi-monthly pubic report on Orange County Public
  Authority (OCPA) activities and updates.

  Dee Fox, Irvine resident, spoke in opposition to the community choice energy program.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  7
 Citv Council Minutes  Julv 27.2021

  ADJOURNMENT

  Moved by Gouncilmember Kuo, seconded by Vice Mayor Kim, and unanimously

  OF THE CITY OF IRVINE
